official.deadline_note: No central deadline exists. Each award is advertised separately and carries its own closing date, published on the Ministry's scholarship page, in the newspapers and on the Ministry's social media pages.
official.application_cycle: Rolling - individual awards are advertised separately, each with its own academic-year cycle (e.g. 2026/2027 and 2027/2028 offers)
official.status_note: Every award currently listed on the Ministry's Government of Guyana scholarships page is marked Closed, the most recent being the Guyana-Chile 2026 offer (closing date 30 September 2026) and the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission 2027/2028 offer (closing date 27 September 2026). The Ministry advertises new awards on a rolling basis and no open round is published at present.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The portal states: "A fully funded Government of Guyana scholarship. Beneficiaries receive full tuition and allowances for books, outfit and travelling, and compensation for any other cost associated with the programme." The Ministry adds that "All beneficiaries of donor funded scholarships receive full /partial tuition, allowances and accommodation, depending on the type of scholarships and benefits."
benefits: Full tuition and allowances for books, outfit and travelling, and compensation for any other cost associated with the programme (fully funded Government of Guyana scholarship)
Job security: graduates are bonded by contract and are guaranteed a job within the public sector after completing their studies
Donor-funded awards: full or partial tuition, allowances and accommodation, depending on the type of scholarship and its benefits
Awards span undergraduate, technical and vocational education, and postgraduate categories based on national workforce requirements
eligibility: Applicants must be a holder of a valid Guyanese Passport
Applicants must have an Unconditional Acceptance Letter from the relevant university, or gain admission to the institute named in the advertisement
Overseas Master's applicants must hold a relevant Bachelor's Degree with a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0
Guyana-Chile applicants must be fluent in the Spanish Language, i.e. able to speak, read and write in Spanish
Age limits are set per award, for example 35 years or under for the Japan, Indonesia and China postgraduate offers and 25 years or under for the China undergraduate and Cuba offers
Current technical institute students must have passes in all completed courses
requirements: Register on the Government of Guyana online scholarship portal and submit the application - all applications are fully online and only available to registered users
Hold admission, or an unconditional acceptance letter, from the institution named in the advertisement
Hold the academic qualification and minimum grade point average named for that award
Meet any language requirement named in the advertisement, for example fluency in Spanish for the Guyana to Chile scholarships
Accept the contractual bond that obliges you to work in the public sector after graduating
documents: Unconditional acceptance letter from the relevant university, or proof of admission to the institute
Academic certificates and transcripts evidencing the qualification and minimum GPA named for the award
Caribbean Secondary Examination Council (CSEC) and Caribbean Advanced Proficiency Examination (CAPE) results for undergraduate offers, where named in the advertisement
selection_criteria: Requirements differ by award and are stated in the advertisement for each scholarship
Awards are offered in three categories - undergraduate, technical and vocational education, and postgraduate - based on national workforce requirements
The academic qualification and minimum GPA named for that award, for example a Bachelor's degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0 for the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission awards
For technical institute offers, admission to the institute plus passes in all completed courses for current students
coverage: Allowances for books, outfit and travelling
Compensation for any other cost associated with the programme
For donor-funded scholarships, full or partial tuition, allowances and accommodation depending on the type of scholarship
application_method: Watch the Ministry's scholarship page, the newspaper advertisements and the Ministry's social media pages for the opening of the relevant award
Open the Scholarship service page on the Government of Guyana portal and use its 'Apply online' link to reach the scholarship application portal
Register as a user, complete the online application and upload the documents named in the specific advertisement
official.application_route: Apply online through the Government of Guyana scholarship application portal reached from the 'Apply online' button on the portal's Scholarship service page; each award has its own advertisement and its own closing date.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be holders of a valid Guyanese passport
official.international_eligibility: No - awards are for Guyanese nationals holding a valid Guyanese passport
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The field of study is fixed by each individual advertisement and reflects national workforce requirements, for example data science and digital transformation, climate smart agriculture, structural, marine, water and wastewater engineering for the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission 2027/2028 round; catering and commercial food preparation for the Carnegie School of Home Economics offers
official.duration: Duration of the advertised programme, for example Master's degree level for the overseas offers and certificate or diploma level for the technical institute and vocational offers
official.description: The Ministry of the Public Service, Government Efficiency and Implementation advertises and administers Government of Guyana scholarships in three categories - undergraduate, technical and vocational education, and postgraduate - based on national workforce requirements. Beneficiaries receive full tuition plus allowances for books, outfit and travelling, and graduates are bonded by contract and guaranteed a job in the public sector after completing their studies.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (national scheme administered by the Ministry of Public Service, Government Efficiency and Implementation)

verification.notes: No award amount, currency or cadence is published on the portal service page, the Ministry scholarship page or the Ministry's main scholarship section, so no figure is asserted. Coverage wording, the bond and the three-category structure were read directly from those official pages; every award on the Ministry page is currently marked Closed.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not one scholarship but a rolling series of separately advertised awards, so the practical task is monitoring the Ministry's scholarship page and the newspapers for an advertisement that matches your qualification. Nothing here is a form you can fill in on a fixed annual date: each award opens and closes on its own schedule, and the last several rounds closed between March and September 2026. Budget your preparation around having a valid Guyanese passport and an unconditional acceptance letter in hand before an advert appears, because most awards ask for both at the point of application. Remember that accepting an award means signing a bond that commits you to public sector service afterwards, so treat it as a career decision and not just a funding decision.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Guyanese nationals who already hold, or can realistically secure, an unconditional offer from the named institution and who are willing to serve in the Guyanese public sector on a contract after graduating.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the Ministry's Government of Guyana scholarships page at least weekly and set a standing alert on mps.gov.gy, since awards appear and close with only weeks of notice
Confirm your Guyanese passport is valid well beyond the expected programme start date, and renew it now if it is not
Line up your transcripts and certificates as clean scans so you can attach them the day an advert opens
Register on the online scholarship portal and verify you can log in before the round you want opens

Read each advert for its own age cap, GPA floor and language rule - the Japan, Indonesia and China postgraduate offers all set 35 years or under and a 3.0 GPA, while the Chile offers add Spanish fluency
Read the bond terms and be certain you accept a public sector service obligation before you submit
common_rejection_risks: Applying to an award whose age cap you have already passed - the caps differ by award (25, 35, or below 40 as of a stated date for Azerbaijan) and are set at the time of application
Supplying a conditional or provisional acceptance letter where the advert requires an unconditional one
Missing a language condition, most obviously the requirement to speak, read and write Spanish for the Guyana-Chile awards
Falling short of the 3.0 GPA floor on a 4-point-style transcript where your grading scale does not translate straightforwardly
Waiting for an advert in your field instead of applying to the nearest eligible discipline - the fields are fixed and narrow
Not being registered on the portal when a short window opens, so losing days to account setup
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award is published as fully funded, covering full tuition plus allowances for books, outfit and travelling and compensation for any other programme cost, so no specific uncovered cost is identified. Donor-funded awards, however, are published as full or partial depending on the award, so confirm in writing which cover applies and what the 'other cost' compensation reaches - insurance, relocation and visa costs for overseas awards are not named in the published wording.
document_audit: Your passport must be valid, not merely present - an expired or soon-expiring passport will not satisfy the advert condition
The acceptance letter must be unconditional; an offer conditional on funding or on results will not meet the requirement
Transcripts must evidence the GPA named in the advert, so obtain a grading scale explanation if your institution does not report a 4.0-style GPA
CSEC and CAPE results are needed for the undergraduate offers, including the minimum five CSEC subjects inclusive of English Language and Mathematics with Grades I or II
For continuing technical institute students, evidence of passes in all completed courses is required
alerts: Every award listed on the Ministry page is currently marked Closed, so treat any plan built on this scheme as dependent on a new advertisement appearing
Closing dates in recent rounds fell as early as March and as late as September, so there is no predictable annual window to plan around
The bond and the guaranteed public sector job are contractual - check what service period and terms are attached before you accept
Donor-funded awards under the same umbrella can be partial, so do not assume the fully funded wording applies to every advertisement you see
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Spot an advertisement, register or log in on the online scholarship portal, complete the online application for that specific award, upload the named documents, and wait for the Ministry's published outcome; there is no single annual intake.
